analysis.one_liner: Zydus Lifesciences makes generic and branded medicines for the US and Indian markets, plus consumer wellness products and specialty/biosimilar drugs.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter ended Sept 2026) are due around November 4-13, 2026 (sources disagree on the exact date), putting the company inside its results blackout window right now. The last reported quarter (Q1 FY27, June 2026) showed revenue up 22% year-on-year to about ₹8,020 crore, but profit fell roughly 35% to ₹940 crore as EBITDA margin compressed sharply from 31.8% to 24.1%. The company also disclosed a USFDA Form 483 with 5 observations at its Moraiya plant (October 2026) and an earlier warning letter concerning talc quality at its Baddi facility - not verified beyond news reports, check FDA.gov for primary confirmation.
analysis.plain_terms: This company sells medicines in the US and India and has been a strong long-term stock performer. But the most recent quarter had an uncomfortable mismatch: sales grew nicely, yet profit dropped by a third. That is not because the business is shrinking - it is because costs (research spending, staff, and expenses tied to integrating a US acquisition) grew even faster than sales. Management says this is a temporary squeeze, not permanent damage, but that claim has not yet been tested by a second quarter of results.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026): revenue ~₹8,020 cr (+22% YoY), EBITDA ~₹1,929 cr at a 24.1% margin (down from 31.8% a year earlier), PAT ~₹940 cr (-35% YoY), missing analyst estimates of around ₹1,000 cr. A net exceptional expense of ₹18.2 crore was booked (₹109 cr Assertio-acquisition severance plus ₹56 cr US antitrust settlement, partly offset by a ₹147 cr litigation settlement receipt) - small relative to the overall profit decline, so most of the margin compression is real, not an accounting artifact: employee costs rose 38% YoY, other operating expenses rose 48% YoY, and R&D spend rose 32% YoY. Effective tax rate also rose to ~27% due to a UK 'thin-cap' tax rule disallowance. Management (MD Dr Sharvil Patel) called it a strong start to FY27, reiterated FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth with an EBITDA margin of 24% or more, mid-teens India growth, but flagged that the US business will grow only in single digits this year as the high base from earlier complex-generic launches fades. Not verified: FY26 full-year figures (revenue ₹27,148 cr, +16.8%; PAT ₹5,040 cr, +11.4%) and prior-quarter numbers came from secondary sources with some unreconciled labeling - check on Screener.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 13.3% from its August 2024 peak but has clearly outperformed over longer horizons: +11.2% over 1 year versus Nifty's -11.4% and peer Lupin's +0.5%; +95.3% over 3 years versus Nifty's +17.1% and Lupin's +67.3%; +118.0% over 5 years versus Nifty's +24.3% and Lupin's +112.6%. There were two stock splits (2010, 2015) but no demerger or spin-off in the supplied corporate-action data, so there is no hidden distortion requiring adjustment - the current drawdown looks like ordinary volatility (52-week range ₹860-1,215), not a crash.
analysis.valuation_read: Trailing P/E is about 22.8-22.9x and P/B about 4.1x, both consistent with a return on equity near 21%, so the valuation is not obviously demanding relative to profitability - it is a market paying up for a business that has historically earned well above its cost of capital. Whether it is cheap depends on whether the Q1 FY27 margin compression is temporary (as management claims) or a new normal; if margins stay near 24% rather than recovering to the low 30s, the earnings base the P/E is built on would need to be reassessed. Some valuation inputs (EV/EBITDA, exact net debt) carry conflicting figures across sources - not verified precisely, check on Screener.
analysis.growth_read: Growth has been volume-led, not margin-led: revenue is up 22% YoY on new product launches (30-40 planned US launches guided for FY27, 513 cumulative ANDA filings) and a branded portfolio now over 55% of revenue, while margins actually fell this quarter rather than expanding. That combination - top-line growth with profitability under pressure - is the more fragile pattern of the two, since it depends on costs normalizing rather than pricing power holding.
analysis.health_read: ROE of 21.2% and ROCE of 21.1% show profits are generating solid returns on capital, and debt looks moderate (debt/equity roughly 0.42x, net debt under 1x EBITDA by most accounts, though exact net debt figures conflict across sources - not verified, check on Screener). The real risk here is business/execution risk - cost inflation, acquisition integration, and US regulatory findings (Form 483 at Moraiya, a warning letter at Baddi) - rather than financial/solvency risk.
analysis.ownership_read: The Zydus Family Trust (Pankaj, Pritiben and Sharvil Patel as trustees) holds about 75% of the company, a level that has been stable, and no pledging of promoter shares was found in available sources. Institutional ownership is modest - FII holding around 7%, mutual funds around 5% spread across 38 schemes with Parag Parikh Flexi Cap (~2%) and Kotak Flexicap (~1.2%) the largest named holders. No well-known individual ('star') investor appears on the shareholding register.
strengths: Revenue grew 22% YoY in Q1 FY27 to about ₹8,020 crore, continuing a run of double-digit top-line growth
ROE of 21.2% and ROCE of 21.1% indicate efficient use of capital despite the quarter's profit dip
Stock has beaten both the Nifty and peer Lupin over 1, 3 and 5-year periods (e.g. +95% vs Nifty's +17% over 3 years)
Promoter holding stable at ~75% with no pledging found, and a diversifying pipeline including an accepted USFDA BLA for a Keytruda biosimilar and positive US trial data for Saroglitazar
watchpoints: Q1 FY27 PAT fell about 35% YoY as EBITDA margin compressed from 31.8% to 24.1%, driven by real cost increases (R&D +32%, employee costs +38%) rather than mostly one-off items - the next quarter will show if this reverses
USFDA Form 483 (5 observations) at the Moraiya plant in October 2026 and a warning letter concerning talc quality at the Baddi facility add US regulatory risk - not independently verified on FDA.gov
Management itself guided US business growth down to single digits for FY27 as the boost from earlier complex-generic launches fades
Dividend is small and erratic (₹1/share latest versus ₹11/share the year before) with a yield of just 0.09%, so this is not a reliable income holding
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results, due around early-to-mid November 2026, will show whether the EBITDA margin recovers toward management's guided 24%+ range or whether the Q1 FY27 compression persists.
analysis.data_notes: Core Q1 FY27 revenue, EBITDA margin and PAT figures were cross-checked across multiple news sources and management commentary. However, EV/EBITDA, exact net debt, DII shareholding percentage, buyback price, and the precise Q2 FY27 results date all had conflicting figures across sources that could not be reconciled - treat those as indicative only and verify on Screener or the company's BSE/NSE filings before relying on them.
